clues.text: After seven Sabbaths of years, Israel was told to sound the horn throughout the land on the Day of Atonement.
The LORD told Israel to consecrate the fiftieth year and proclaim liberty in the land for all its inhabitants.
In this holy year, Israel was not to sow fields, reap aftergrowth, or harvest untended vines.
Under the law given through Moses, Israelites priced land by the years since this event and the harvests remaining.
A house in a walled city that was not redeemed within a year was not released at this time.
An Israelite who sold himself served as a hired worker until this time, then went free with his children.
The clan heads of Gilead feared that at this time, Zelophehad's daughters' inheritance would pass to other tribes.
